input.args: Issue 714: InjectMocks on a presenter with a package-private non-default constructor (two params: Analytics, PendingActionsProcessor) and a non-final nullable field `view`. Reporter expects `view` to be null after setup and finds that the injection differs from what they expected under Mockito 2.2.0. Evidence: mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/InjectMocks.java (Javadoc: constructor injection runs first, and if it succeeds Mockito won't try property or field injection; static and final fields are ignored); mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/internal/configuration/injection/ConstructorInjection.java (biggest constructor is used, unresolved args get null).

final: {"number": 714, "label": "question", "route": "answer", "related": [195, 352, 1389], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/InjectMocks.java", "mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/internal/configuration/injection/ConstructorInjection.java"], "reply": "Hi, this is documented behaviour of @InjectMocks. Mockito tries constructor injection first. It picks the constructor with the most parameters and resolves each argument from the @Mock and @Spy fields in your test. If that constructor call succeeds, Mockito does not run property or field injection afterwards, so your non-final field `view` is left untouched and stays null. Static and final fields are always skipped. If an argument has no matching mock, Mockito passes null. If you need a specific state before the test runs, create the presenter yourself in a @Before method, or keep calling subscribe(viewMock) as you do now. The details are in the Javadoc of org.mockito.InjectMocks."}
